headlines.headline: Bank of Canada Holds Rate at 4.75% — Warns Renewal Cliff Will Test Borrowers Into 2026
headlines.driver: For ZEB.TO (equal-weight Big Six): Hawkish hold is double-edged — near-term negative because 60% of mortgages renewing 2025-26 face +$420/mo payment shock, lifting performing-loan PCL; longer-term positive because BoC's 4.75% keeps NIM wide (2.07% ex-trading) while stress test prevents solvency event — ZEB trades on NIM vs PCL spread, so hold extends earnings durability, not a multiple re-rating.

headlines.headline: OSFI Keeps Domestic Stability Buffer at 3.5%, Flags High Household Debt Vulnerability
headlines.driver: For ZEB.TO: Neutral to slightly positive — 3.5% buffer hold keeps CET1 hurdle high (RBC 13.5% vs 11.5% minimum) but avoids a hike that would force banks to retain capital instead of paying 4-5% dividend + buybacks (BMO NCIB). Signals regulator sees risk but not systemic — allows ZEB's 6-7% shareholder yield to compound, no de-rating.

headlines.headline: Canadian Housing Starts Fall 9% in May as Pre-Sale Condo Market Cools
headlines.driver: For ZEB.TO: Near-term mild negative — 9% fewer starts = slower mortgage + HELOC origination and fee income for Big Six in GTA condo corridor; offset is long-run positive — tighter supply supports home prices and 58% LTV cushion, limiting loss-given-default. Net: small drag on loan growth this quarter, but protects ZEB's collateral value and keeps future PCL contained — not a sell signal.
